name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,837

entries.clue: Having issue with hearth, cooked boring meal (10)

indicatorNotes.cooked: What comes out of the pan is not in the state it went in, so the letters are served up rearranged.
indicatorNotes.boring: To bore is to drill into something, and what does the drilling ends up inside it.

blocks.note: food is a meal, and it opens after its first letter to take the filling
the six letters of HEARTH in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone has trouble with the fireplace and ends up cooking a dull dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Having issue' is the legal sense of issue, meaning offspring, so the domestic row the surface offers is a decoy. 'Cooked' and 'boring' are two separate instructions, not one.
annotation.definitionFit: Fatherhood is the state of having children, and issue is the old legal word for offspring that wills and crosswords keep alive.

entries.clue: Seafood close to sea bass and sole (7)

indicatorNotes.close to: The close of anything is its end, so what is wanted is the letter that ends the word.

blocks.note: the last letter of SEA
b is the musical abbreviation for bass
sole means alone, the only one

annotation.surface: A fishmonger lists what came in today, alongside sea bass and sole.
annotation.walkthrough: Bass and sole are both fish, which is exactly why neither is a fish here: one is the singing voice, the other is the 'only' sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail, prized on the plate from California to Japan, so seafood is the class it belongs to.

entries.clue: Henry put on pretty dress (5)

indicatorNotes.put on: Putting one thing on another sets it above, and in a down entry whatever sits above is written first.

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
'pretty tired' and 'a bit tired' say the same thing, so pretty = A BIT

annotation.surface: Henry gets himself up in an attractive frock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like a man and is a unit of measurement, the way 'volt' or 'watt' would be. The dress is the one a monk or nun wears.
annotation.definitionFit: A habit is the plain robe worn by a monk or a nun, so dress is clothing in its general sense.

entries.clue: Racecourse favourite gets VIP treatment (3,6)

blocks.note: Redcar is a racecourse in the seaside town of that name in North Yorkshire
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

annotation.surface: At the races the favourite is treated like visiting royalty.
annotation.walkthrough: The racing surface hides a place name, and English courses turn up constantly in clues: Ascot, Epsom, Aintree, Redcar. 'Favourite' looks like the betting sense and means the pampered one.
annotation.definitionFit: Rolling out the red carpet is what a host does for an important guest, so the phrase stands for the whole star welcome.

entries.clue: Somewhat friendly pranks seeming to upset (2,8,5)

indicatorNotes.upset: Upsetting something tips it over and spills its contents out in a fresh arrangement.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: Practical jokes that look as though they are about to cause real trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: The little word 'to' belongs to the letters, not to the instruction, which is where a long anagram like this one usually goes wrong.
annotation.definitionFit: People on speaking terms are civil to each other and no warmer than that, which is the work 'somewhat' is doing.

entries.clue: Things said at police getting twisted (5)

indicatorNotes.getting twisted: Something twisted round has been turned to face the other way, so the letters are read backwards.

blocks.note: taken as it stands
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of a British police force

annotation.surface: Statements made at the police station come out distorted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' promises distorted testimony and delivers a backwards reading. Dicta is the plural of dictum, familiar from the obiter dicta of law reports.
annotation.definitionFit: A dictum is a pronouncement — Latin for a thing said — so dicta are things said, several of them.

entries.clue: Band of elite soldiers back on warpath (4)

indicatorNotes.back: The back of a word is its rear end, which is its final letter.

blocks.note: the SAS, the Special Air Service, is the British army's elite regiment
the final letter of WARPATH

annotation.surface: Crack troops are on the warpath once again.
annotation.walkthrough: A sash is part of ceremonial uniform, so the soldiering fits the answer as well as it fits the wordplay. 'Back' asks for one letter here and is not a reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn round the waist or across one shoulder, which is 'band' in its plainest sense.

entries.clue: Bog went by water on map, near delta (9)

indicatorNotes.on: In a down entry one thing sits on another by being written above it, so the swimming goes in first.

blocks.note: to travel by water under your own power is to swim; the past tense is SWAM
a plan is a scale drawing or map of a place
delta is D in the radio alphabet

annotation.surface: A route is plotted by water, close to the delta shown on the map.
annotation.walkthrough: A river delta really is marshy ground, so the geography of the surface sits next door to the answer; the clue means only the radio-alphabet letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Swampland and bog both name ground so waterlogged that it will not carry a footstep, so the two are straight synonyms.

entries.clue: Special festival's back with yen to spend extravagantly (7)

indicatorNotes.back: A word's back is its tail end, so what is handed over is its last letter.

blocks.note: sp is the standard short form of special
the last letter of FESTIVAL
a yen for something is an urge for it

annotation.surface: A one-off festival has come round again and there is money to burn.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'festival's back' to mean the festival has returned; the wordplay reads it as a possessive. 'Yen' is the appetite, not the currency, which would have handed over a lone Y.
annotation.definitionFit: To splurge is to lay money out freely on something indulgent, which is spending extravagantly under another name.

entries.clue: Spotted flatfish at bottom of river (6)

blocks.note: a dab is a small flatfish of the plaice family
the bottom of a river is its bed

annotation.surface: A flatfish is sighted lying on the riverbed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of' normally asks for a final letter, so the R of 'river' is the trap; the setter wants the whole riverbed instead.
annotation.definitionFit: To dab paint on is to apply it in small spots, so a surface that has been dabbed has been spotted.

entries.clue: Warm fur coats start to outsell cold one (8)

indicatorNotes.coats: A coat goes right round what it covers, so the fur closes round the letters it is given.
indicatorNotes.start to: The start of a word is the letter it opens with.

blocks.note: sable is the dark fur of the marten of that name
the first letter of OUTSELL
c is cold, the marking on a tap
I is one in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: In a coat shop, warm fur is beginning to outsell something lighter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coats' looks like the garments the shop is selling and is in fact the verb, and what it wraps round is three unrelated single letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A sociable person is warm in the friendly sense, the warmth of good company rather than of temperature.

entries.clue: Stole evidence in Oxbridge row? (4,4)

blocks.note: a boa is a long stole of fur or feathers worn round the neck
a trace of something is the evidence it leaves behind

annotation.surface: Someone made off with the proof during a university rowing contest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stole' is the garment rather than the theft the sentence sets up. The question mark is doing real work: the answer is one particular row, not rows in general.
annotation.definitionFit: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford against Cambridge contest on the Thames, so the definition names it by example, with row in its rowing sense.

entries.clue: Hope is a small, quiet emotion (6)

blocks.note: taken as it stands
s is the clothing size small
p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
ire is anger, one emotion among many

annotation.surface: Hope painted as a small, quiet feeling.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes hope sound like a modest little emotion, which hides the fact that the answer is a verb: something you do rather than something you have.
annotation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope for something and reach towards it, so the verb 'hope' drops straight into its place.

entries.clue: Betray group of spies as dictator (4)

indicatorNotes.as dictator: A dictator is someone saying words out loud for another to write down, so this word is heard rather than spelt.

blocks.note: a cell is a small group of agents working together, and said aloud it gives the answer

annotation.surface: A ring of spies is handed over to the tyrant in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' is the person dictating words for someone else to take down, not the tyrant the spy story suggests. Sound and spelling differ by a single letter here.
annotation.definitionFit: To sell someone is to betray them for your own advantage, as in selling out a friend.

entries.clue: Eleventh-hour comeback using creative thinking (9)

blocks.note: an eleventh-hour decision is a late one
a side that rallies stages a comeback

annotation.surface: A team leaves it to the last minute and then stages a recovery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Comeback' looks like an instruction to reverse and is nothing of the sort, being the sporting recovery. Lateral thinking is Edward de Bono's term for attacking a problem from the side.
annotation.definitionFit: To work laterally is to come at a problem sideways instead of head-on, which is what creative thinking means here.

entries.clue: Bluffer's expression perfect when holding decent card (5,4)

indicatorNotes.holding: To hold something is to keep it inside you, so the holding letters close round the held ones.

blocks.note: perf is the grammarian's short form of perfect, as in the perfect tense
OK means decent, good enough
an ace is a playing card

annotation.surface: A card player gives nothing away while sitting on a strong hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Holding' is the poker word the surface leans on and the container instruction underneath it. PERF is the abbreviation grammar books use for the perfect tense.
annotation.definitionFit: A poker face is the blank look worn so that nobody can read the hand behind it, which is exactly what a bluffer needs.

entries.clue: Runner smuggles ketamine and ecstasy for dodgy dealer (9)

indicatorNotes.smuggles: Smuggling is carrying goods concealed inside, so what is smuggled sits within the carrier's letters.

blocks.note: a racer is a runner
ket is the street name for ketamine
E is ecstasy

annotation.surface: An athlete carries drugs on behalf of a shady supplier.
annotation.walkthrough: The drug-squad surface does the misdirecting: a runner there is a courier, while the wordplay wants nothing but plain athletics.
annotation.definitionFit: A racketeer lives off organised crime — extortion, protection, black-market trade — so 'dodgy dealer' catches the crooked line of business.

entries.clue: In a stupor, Tom perhaps needs a pick-me-up (9)

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat, and 'perhaps' flags one example of the general word
taken as it stands
a tonic is a pick-me-up

annotation.surface: A listless cat called Tom could do with something to perk him up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tom perhaps' is the crossword way of pointing at a cat through one of them. The stupor is the cat's in the surface and a clinical condition in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone catatonic is rigid and unresponsive, the stupor being the psychiatric state the word names.

entries.clue: Directs Rocky titles (7)

indicatorNotes.Rocky: Rocky ground is uneven and unsteady, and letters on unsteady footing will not keep their order.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Somebody directs the film Rocky.
annotation.walkthrough: The italics dress 'Rocky' up as a film title and stand it beside 'Directs' as though both belonged to cinema, while its real job is to unsettle those seven letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A film's credits are the lists of names that roll at either end of it, known in the trade as the titles.

entries.clue: Couple performing outstanding tango (4)

blocks.note: a bill still outstanding is one that is due
tango is T in the radio alphabet

annotation.surface: A pair dance a magnificent tango.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' is the accountant's word here, meaning unpaid, rather than the praise the dancers are being offered.
annotation.definitionFit: A duet is a piece written for two performers, so a couple performing together are giving one.

entries.clue: Beheaded queens wrongly over sex in private washroom (2,5)

indicatorNotes.Beheaded: Beheading takes off the head, and a word's head is the letter it begins with.
indicatorNotes.wrongly: Letters set down wrongly are letters in the wrong order.
indicatorNotes.over: One thing laid over another covers it, so these letters close round what they cover.

blocks.note: QUEENS loses its head, the Q, and the five letters left are rearranged
'it' is the coy old word for sex

annotation.surface: Queens are wrongly executed over a sex scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beheaded' reads as Tudor history next to 'queens', which is the trap; it is the ordinary instruction to drop a first letter. 'It' for sex is old slang that crosswords keep in circulation.
annotation.definitionFit: An en suite is a bathroom opening straight off one bedroom and used by whoever sleeps there, so it is private by design.

entries.clue: Pointillist surfaces on some unfamiliar art (6)

indicatorNotes.surfaces: The surfaces of a thing are its outsides, so each word gives up the letters on its outside.

blocks.note: the outside letters of SOME
the outside letters of UNFAMILIAR
the outside letters of ART

annotation.surface: A pointillist's painted surfaces turn up on a piece of art nobody recognises.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Surfaces' looks like the noun a painter works on, canvas and board, and is asking instead for the outside of each word after it. Seurat built his pictures from dots of pure colour.
annotation.definitionFit: Georges Seurat invented pointillism, so the word for the technique names him by the method he worked in.

entries.clue: He sings relatively high note for audience (5)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition describes the man instead of naming him: the singer whose voice sits relatively high is a tenor.

indicatorNotes.for audience: Anything done for an audience is meant to be heard, so the word is spoken rather than written.

blocks.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note in Britain, and said aloud it gives the answer

annotation.surface: A singer holds a high note in front of a crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' is the banknote and not the musical one, which is the trap in a clue otherwise full of singing. Tenor and tenner are all but identical in most English accents.
annotation.definitionFit: A tenor is the high male voice, pitched above the baritone and bass, so a man singing up there is one.

entries.clue: Nancy's very flirtatious act causes offence (8)

blocks.note: Nancy is a city in France, so the word wanted is the French très
to make a pass at someone is to make a flirtatious advance

annotation.surface: A forward piece of flirting in Nancy leaves somebody insulted.
annotation.walkthrough: A French place name in a clue is usually telling you to change language, and Nancy's word for 'very' is très.
annotation.definitionFit: A trespass is a wrongdoing, the sense kept alive in 'forgive us our trespasses' alongside the land-law meaning.

entries.clue: On the counter is energy drink (5)

indicatorNotes.On the counter: To run counter to something is to go the opposite way, so these letters are read in the opposite direction.

blocks.note: taken as it stands
pep is energy, vigour

annotation.surface: Something energising is standing on the shop counter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' plays on the counter a bottle stands on and on over-the-counter goods, while its real job is to turn the letters round.
annotation.definitionFit: Pepsi is a brand of cola, so the definition names the class the trade name belongs to.

entries.clue: Military ship worker who might deal with Green Berets (8)

annotation.definition: worker who might deal with Green Berets

blocks.note: mil is the everyday short form of military
a liner is a large passenger ship

annotation.surface: A crewman on a warship has dealings with the US special forces.
annotation.walkthrough: Capital letters are free in a surface, and these two turn hats into a regiment. Everything before 'worker' is the wordplay, everything after it is the joke.
annotation.definitionFit: A milliner makes and sells hats, so green berets are stock in the shop rather than the American special forces the capitals suggest.

entries.clue: Dash of medium strength liquor ultimately vermouth (6)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: What comes ultimately is what comes last, so the word gives up its final letter.

blocks.note: a medium's claimed strength is ESP, extrasensory perception
the last letter of LIQUOR
It is Italian vermouth, the It of a gin and It

annotation.surface: A measure of middling spirits is finished off with vermouth.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is a drinks order, which is why 'medium' reads as a strength; the medium wanted is the one at the seance. Gin and It was the fashionable cocktail of the 1920s.
annotation.definitionFit: Esprit is the French word English borrowed for wit and liveliness, and dash is that same spirit and flair.

entries.clue: Upsilon and psi reversed in guessing game (1-3)

indicatorNotes.reversed: Reversed means turned back to front, so the letters are read from the far end.

blocks.note: upsilon is the Greek letter English writes as Y
the Greek letter psi, spelt out in full

annotation.surface: Two Greek letters written down back to front.
annotation.walkthrough: Greek letters go into wordplay in either of two ways, and this clue uses both: upsilon as the single letter it stands for, psi as its name spelt out.
annotation.definitionFit: I-spy is the children's guessing game — 'I spy with my little eye' — where one player gives a letter and the rest guess the object.

entries.clue: Checked others showered (10)

blocks.note: the rest of a group is the others
it showered and it rained say the same thing of the weather

annotation.surface: Someone checked that everybody else had washed.
annotation.walkthrough: The bathroom reading of 'showered' is the trap, and the answer needs the weather one instead. Three words are all the setter gives you here.
annotation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it — a temper checked, a horse checked — which is what restrained means.
